This page tracks the most important missing records in the CSIL history. A September 2026 public-source review looked for independent evidence that each item existed and recorded what was found.

**Four source groups remain open.** A wanted record is not an inspected text: follow the catalogue link for the evidence supporting its existence, the searches already attempted, and the unresolved questions.

## 1. Creekview 202 Project Evaluation Report

A formal Creekview evaluation is independently supported by a 1987 PubMed abstract and Haw's 1989 overview. The report itself has not been recovered.

- **Date:** about 1987
- **Authorship:** unresolved. Early project notes name Patricia Ryan / Ryan & Wiggins; inspected sources instead refer to a government-and-CPA or independent evaluation.
- **Useful leads:** the full *Dimensions in Health Service* article, library records, ministry correspondence, and Canadian Paraplegic Association project files
- **Record:** [Creekview 202 Project Evaluation Report](../sources/wanted-creekview-202-evaluation.qmd)

## 2. *Keys on Freedom*

Early project notes describe a resource manual called *Keys on Freedom: Resource manual for the development of self-managed community living alternatives for quadriplegic persons*, attributed to BC Rehabilitation Society around 1990.

No independent public record confirming the title, author, or year has yet been found.

- **Record:** [*Keys on Freedom*](../sources/wanted-keys-on-freedom.qmd)

## 3. Enhanced Consumer Participation Model (ECPM) manual(s)

A Roeher / Salisbury bibliography independently lists a 1990 *Enhanced Consumer Participation Model: Skill Development Manual for Consumers of Home Support Services*, produced by BC Rehab and Greater Vancouver Home Support Society. The manual itself has not been recovered.

A possible 1994 revision remains unconfirmed, as does any title-page role for Emma Van der Klift.

- **Finding aid:** [Roeher / Salisbury bibliography](../sources/1990s-roeher-if-bibliography.qmd)
- **Narrative:** [ECPM chapter](../history/ecpm.qmd)
- **Record:** [ECPM manual(s)](../sources/wanted-ecpm-manuals.qmd)

## 4. Original Ministry of Health CSIL pilot/design records

These are the most important missing records for establishing how CSIL was designed and introduced in the early 1990s.

Later sources disagree about timing: Paul Gauthier materials use 1993 or 1994; the 2012 Ombudsperson report describes a **1994 pilot** and **1995 province-wide availability**; the late-1995 HEU *Guardian* still described CSIL as new or a pilot within the Community Support Branch / Continuing Care Division.

The archive needs original ministry records from approximately 1993–95 to clarify what each date represented, who participated in the design, and how the pilot moved into a broader program.

- **Narrative:** [CSIL design and pilot](../history/csil-pilot.qmd)
- **Record:** [Ministry CSIL pilot/design records](../sources/wanted-ministry-csil-pilot-records.qmd)

## Recovered: 2008 CSIL Program Review Synthesis Report

The November 2008 *Choice in Supports for Independent Living (CSIL) Program Review: Synthesis Report* is no longer a wanted source. A Microlog fiche is publicly inspectable on Internet Archive.

- **Prepared by:** James Murtagh Consulting for Home and Community Care Branch, Health Authorities Division, BC Ministry of Health Services
- **Public copy:** [Internet Archive Microlog fiche](https://archive.org/details/micro_IA40244204_0972)
- **Catalogue record:** [2008 Program Review Synthesis Report](../sources/2008-program-review-synthesis.qmd)

The report says only that CSIL dates to “the 1990's”; it does not settle the 1993-versus-1994 question. The Ombudsperson's reference to a “provincial review in 2007” also remains to be reconciled with this November 2008 synthesis.

## Search status

Public web, PubMed, BC Hansard, the HEU *Guardian* archive, the B.C. Ombudsperson site, Internet Archive, government sites, SCI BC, IFRC, Governor General honours material, and several bibliographic searches have been checked. Native catalogues at UBC, SFU, the Legislative Library of British Columbia, and the CMHC Housing Knowledge Centre remain useful next steps.

Detailed search notes belong in the individual wanted-source records rather than being repeated here.

## If you have a lead

Open a GitHub issue describing the item and where a public copy might be found. Do **not** email or attach files of uncertain copyright, and do not send private or health-related records. See the [copyright policy](../docs/copyright-policy.qmd).
